description: Posit Connect client contract shared by pkg-r and pkg-py. The source is tests/shared/connect.json; the copy under pkg-r/tests/testthat/fixtures/shared/ is generated by scripts/sync-shared.sh. Edit the source and re-run that script.

environment.description: Environment variables the client reads. A publisher or Connect itself sets these, so both packages must read the same names.

server_normalization.description: Server URLs a publisher might configure, and the base each reduces to. Publishers paste whatever the dashboard shows them, so a form one package accepts and the other does not sends requests to the wrong place.

api_request.description: Where a request lands, given the normalized server and the path segments the caller passes. Both packages address Connect's versioned API root.

collaborator_grant.description: The permission commons creates so a user can read this content's trajectories. Reading traces needs editor-level access, and Connect's permissions API spells that role "owner"; it rejects "editor". A lesser permission on the content, such as the viewer role someone gets when the app is shared with them, does not carry trace access, so it is not a reason to skip them.

sharing.description: Who gets a grant, given the usernames asked for and the permissions that already exist on the content. `permitted` is the permissions response, and `expected` lists the principals granted, in order. Connect answers a grant for a principal in `refused` with a 4xx, as it does for the content's owner or an account that cannot publish. A case with `warns` set expects a warning. Test doubles resolve username `x` to principal `guid-x`, except a username in `unknown`, which no Connect user has.

cases.name: a user with no permission is granted one
a user who already holds the role is left alone
a user with only viewer access is still granted the role
only the user missing the role is granted
a username is matched regardless of case
case variants of one username are granted once
a permissions object rather than a list grants nobody
a user Connect refuses does not stop the grants after it
an unknown username does not stop the grants after it

sharing_again.description: Which usernames a second share in the same process looks up on Connect. Each case shares with `usernames`, then with `again`. `looked_up` lists the usernames the second share looks up, and `granted` the principals it grants. A grant that went through is not repeated. A refused one is tried again, so a fix the publisher makes on Connect takes effect when the agent is next built. Connect refuses a grant for a principal in `refused` during the first share only.

cases.name: a granted user is not looked up again, in any case
a refused user is looked up again

traces.description: Reading a content item's trace lines. A read pages through the content's `traces` endpoint with `limit` set to `page_size` and `offset` set to the number of lines read so far, until a page is empty, `X-Total-Count` is not a number, or the offset reaches it. On a server older than `legacy_store_before`, as its `Server` header gives it, the read may stop paging once the caller has enough (see `enough` in trajectories/connect.json). Otherwise, and when the version is unknown, the read also reads each job's own store: the content's `jobs`, then each job's `jobs/<key>/traces` endpoint, paged the same way with `since` in place of `from` and no `to`, a page from each unfinished job in turn. A line read from both stores is kept once, at its first place. When the `traces` endpoint answers 404, the job stores alone are read. 401 or 403 from the `traces` or `jobs` endpoints, or from a job's traces endpoint, is an access error whose message begins with `access_error`. 404 from the `jobs` endpoint means the server has no such content, an error whose message begins with `missing_error` and names `guid` and `server`. A job whose traces endpoint answers 404 is skipped. Any other failure is an error. `since` and `until` are in seconds since the epoch and are sent as trajectories/connect.json's `window_param` gives. Each case reads the content `guid` from `server`, and paths are relative to `/__api__/v1/content/<guid>/`.
traces.access_error: Couldn't read this content's traces from Posit Connect.
traces.missing_error: Can't find this content on Posit Connect.
traces.double: The Connect double a case reads from, given as each case's `server`. `version` sets the `Server` header to `Posit Connect v<version>`, or leaves it out when absent. `traces` lists the lines the `traces` endpoint serves, newest first, or gives `{status}` for an endpoint that answers with that status. A response holds the lines from the request's offset, at most `page_size` of them when it is set, each followed by a newline, with `X-Total-Count` set to the number of lines, or to `total` when the case gives it. `jobs` lists the content's jobs, each a `key` with `traces` served the same way, or gives `{status}`; absent means no jobs. `enough` true means the caller always has enough. `requests` lists each request as its path and its query, compared without regard to order, since job pages may be fetched concurrently. `lines` is the result, in order, and `error` is `access`, `missing`, or `failed` when the read fails.

the window is sent padded
an old server stops once the caller has enough
a newer server reads every page whatever the caller has

vanity_search.description: Finding the content a vanity URL names. The read searches content at `search/content` with `request`'s query, `q` set to the name, and `page_number` counting from 1. It takes the guid of the first result whose `vanity_url` is the server joined to the name by one slash, comparing both without a query, a fragment, or trailing slashes, and percent-decoded. A result without a `vanity_url` never matches. It reads the next page until `page_number` reaches the answer's `total`, and stops when the answer has none. When nothing matches, the read fails (`expected` is null). `pages` are the search's answers, by page number. `page_numbers` lists the page each request asked for.

an answer without a total ends the search
